subject: Operating Systems
title: Discover FCFS Scheduling
description: Discover how the CPU runs ready processes in their arrival order.

mission.title: Run the Ready Queue
mission.description: Follow each process from the ready queue to the CPU and then to completion.

quiz.question: In FCFS scheduling, which process runs first?

discovery.title: Arrival Order Decides
discovery.summary: FCFS scheduling runs processes in the same order they arrive in the ready queue.

sections.title: What is a process?
sections.content: A process is a program that is currently ready to run or is running on the computer.

sections.title: What is CPU scheduling?
sections.content: CPU scheduling decides which ready process gets to use the CPU next.

sections.title: Ready queue
sections.content: The ready queue holds processes that are waiting for CPU time.

sections.title: What is FCFS?
sections.content: FCFS means First Come, First Served.

sections.title: Arrival order
sections.content: Processes run in the same order that they arrive in the ready queue.

sections.title: Advantage
sections.content: FCFS is simple to understand and easy to implement.

sections.title: Disadvantage
sections.content: A long process at the front can make short processes wait for a long time.

sections.title: Convoy effect
sections.content: The convoy effect happens when many short processes are stuck waiting behind one long process, like cars behind a slow truck.
